exercise1.prompt: Smoothing a noisy series to see the shape underneath.

hiddenCases.name: a window of one changes nothing
a window as long as the series gives one value

exercise1.hint: s.rolling(window).mean() gives the smoothed series with gaps at the front; dropna() removes them and tolist() hands back plain floats.

questions.prompt: Why do the first values of a rolling mean come back missing?
choices: There are not enough earlier values to fill the window yet
questions.explain: A window of seven has no answer until the seventh value. Filling those with zero would invent a dip that never happened.

questions.prompt: What is a seven-day rolling mean good for on daily data?
choices: Removing the weekday pattern so the trend is visible
questions.explain: A whole week per window averages out the weekly rhythm, which is usually noise relative to the question.

questions.prompt: What does a larger window do to the line?
choices: Makes it smoother and slower to react
questions.explain: Smoothing is a trade: more window is less noise and more lag behind a real turn.
